newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vereinsbank unit sees bank shares peaking.
newsitem.headline: Vereinsbank unit sees bank shares peaking.

text.p: The top official of a Bayerische Vereinsbank AG subsidiary said on Thursday he expected that German bank share prices had peaked but that he saw scope for further increases in insurance industry shares.

Udo Bandow, chief executive of Vereins-und Westbank AG, said: "If I look at the share price development in recent weeks, I have the impression that the main share price rise of the banks lies behind us. I see a little more scope in the insurance sector."
German banking stocks have recently surged amid merger speculation following news that Vereinsbank and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG (Hypo-Bank) will merge.
As part of the merger, Vereinsbank will exchange most of its 10 percent stake in insurer Allianz AG for a stake of up to 45 percent in Hypo-Bank.
Bandow said the move would significantly increase the liquidity of Allianz shares.

Responding to fears that the exchange could put Allianz shares intially under pressure, Bandow said that investment banks Dresdner Kleinwort Benson and Goldman Sachs had formed a group which would place any surplus of Allianz shares with domestic and international investors.
Vereins-und Westbank is carrying out the exchange of Allianz shares on behalf of Vereinsbank.
